Performers
Nanny Larsen-⁠Todsen (soprano — Isolde), Bayreuth Festival Orchestra (orchestra), Karl Elmendorff (conductor) Documented

The sleeve explicitly assigns these ensemble/conductor credits to the Liebestod, unlike conductors listed for other album tracks.

[2]
Work version
Act III closing scene with soprano, “Mild und leise” Documented

Not the orchestra-only concert arrangement. The exact performing edition and any retouching are not identified.

[1] [2]
Recorded
1928-08 Inferred, not documented

The sleeve documents 1928. The matching Elmendorff/Bayreuth matrix series is dated August 1928 by the Naxos inlay; no exact day is supplied.

[2] [3]
Place
Wagner Theater, Bayreuth Inferred, not documented

Linked through the matching 1928 Columbia matrix series; the Preiser sleeve itself identifies the orchestra but not the room.

[2] [3]
Label
Columbia; transferred reissue: Preiser Lebendige Vergangenheit Documented

The uploaded track is presented as a transfer of Preiser LP LV 174, side A, track 3, not a direct fresh transfer of the original Columbia discs.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
Original Columbia L 2206; reissue Preiser LV 174 Documented

Original and reissue numbers describe different carriers.

[1] [2]
Matrix, take, sides
AX 3986/87 (Preiser sleeve); WAX 3986/87 (Naxos original matrix list) Disputed: sources disagree

The source sleeve omits the initial W used in the fuller discographic matrix list. Two sides are identified by the consecutive matrix numbers; take suffixes are not established.

  • AX 3986/87
  • WAX 3986/87
[2] [3]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No transfer engineer is identified; an uploader is not automatically the engineer.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The upload date is not treated as a transfer date.

[1]
Processing
Archive supplies a 160 kbps MP3 derivative of the uploaded WAV. Documented

No restoration engineer or editing process is credited for this transfer. Ward Marston’s credit on the separate Naxos release is not imported.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Wagner died in 1883. This is a term calculation, not worldwide clearance of every edition.

[1]
Recording rights
Archive marks this recording Public Domain; the historical 1928 Columbia issue also falls within the project’s pre-1963 EU recording rule. Documented

Territorial: EU status is relied on, not worldwide public-domain status. US status is not established; the 1928 recording does not meet the US pre-1926 cutoff. The PDM URL describes a status claim, not a newly granted copyright licence.

[1] [2]

Wagner: Liebestod; Nanny Larsen-⁠Todsen, Bayreuth Festival Orchestra, Karl Elmendorff, 1928. Columbia L 2206, via Preiser LV 174 and Internet Archive. Archive Public Domain Mark; EU territorial basis; US status not established. Rights statement
